finding.statement: The earlier finding that Great Berkhamsted held no Gurney burial at any date was produced by two query defects, each of which fails closed - returning zero rather than an error - and both generalise. First, a wildcard on the stem 'gurn' cannot reach 'Gourney', and the Berkhamsted family is indexed in the burial set predominantly under Gourney; the five seventeenth-century Gourney burials were invisible to the query that reported zero. Second, the place token differs between sets of the same county: the baptism set and the cross-collection view label the parish 'Great Berkhampstead', while the burial set labels it 'Berkhamstead', and because the keyword is a literal token match, both spellings tried earlier returned zero from a parish that is fully present. The project's own record already held the correction in two places - the source registry's note on the Hertfordshire burial set, recording a walk of 9 May 2026 that found Jhon Gourney burials of 1612 and 1620, and the identity assessment's own prose. A sweep contradicted both and reported the contradiction as a discovery. That is the mechanism the 'documented but never assembled' probability row describes, observed inside this project's own work.
